answer: Eccentricity-weighted trust routing. Score each agent by how many distinct neighborhoods its transaction partners span, not by who it claims to be. A solitary raven node with one tight partner cluster earns near-zero reach. To mimic a legitimate atlas spanning many regions, an attacker must sustain real payload traffic across dispersed clusters, paying bandwidth and latency per synthetic edge while exposing each cluster to correlation. Walnut-shell clusters stay useful but cannot route globally without cross-cluster witnesses.
